name: Men's BB cream use

card.summary: Men's BB cream use is the wearing of a tinted blemish balm, popular in Korea, to even out skin tone and cover blemishes with a natural look.
card.note: Product and skin-tone match vary by brand.

quick.overview:
BB cream, short for blemish balm, is an all-in-one tinted product combining foundation, moisturiser and sunscreen. Men use it to even out skin tone and soften redness or blemishes without the heavier look of foundation.

It was first formulated in Germany in the 1960s to protect skin after peels and surgery, then developed for daily use in South Korea in the 1980s. Some Korean brands, and some foreign ones, sell versions aimed at men.
quick.how: Users apply a thin layer to the face as part of a daily routine, often in place of separate foundation and moisturiser. It is described as a lighter alternative to heavier Western foundations.
quick.risks: Risks are those of any cosmetic: possible skin irritation or clogged pores for some people, and shade mismatch. Sources describing it do not report specific hazards.

lead: BB cream is an all-in-one tinted product that combines foundation, moisturiser and sunscreen; BB stands for blemish balm, blemish base or beauty balm.[1] Men use it for an even skin tone and covered blemishes with a natural finish.[1]

It was first formulated in the 1960s by German dermatologist Christine Schrammek for post-peel and post-surgery skin, then developed for daily commercial use in South Korea in the 1980s, with Korean and Japanese markets adopting it from 1985.[1]

Wikipedia, citing 2010 and 2012 Korea Times articles, notes that some Korean brands offer BB creams for men, and Lab Series, a non-Korean brand, makes one too.[1] BB creams made up 13% of the South Korean cosmetics market in 2011.[1]

angle.text: The tint evens skin tone and conceals blemishes while the moisturising and sunscreen components cover basic care, giving a natural-looking complexion.

paras: BB cream is positioned as a multi-purpose product, and Korean women often use it in place of heavier foundations.[1]
It originated in German dermatology, was commercialised in Korea in the 1980s, and Western companies launched versions in 2012.[1]
Male lines exist from several brands, per Korea Times coverage cited by Wikipedia.[1]

timeline.event: Formulated in Germany by Christine Schrammek.[1]
Korean and Japanese markets adopt BB cream.[1]
Western companies begin launching BB creams.[1]
